extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers developing/evaluating LLMs for patent drafting, and IP/patent professionals interested in automated patent-generation quality
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating large language models' ability to generate patentable concept texts and IP-related outputs using automated metrics, specialized IP benchmarks, human/LLM judges, and case-study qualitative criteria (title/abstract/claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Exam
rubrics_metrics.description: A custom benchmark derived from multiple-choice Q&A content used in the U.S. Patent Bar Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher performance indicates a model’s capability to not only understand but also accurately apply IP law principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Quiz
rubrics_metrics.description: An IP-related benchmark task included in the 'Patent Bench' that tests domain knowledge relevant to intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside IP_Exam, IP_Match, and MMLU to profile model performance on IP-specific tasks (Table 7 / Fig. 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Match
rubrics_metrics.description: An IP-related benchmark task in the Patent Bench suite measuring the model's ability to distinguish or match IP-related items (e.g., patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the four Patent Bench evaluation tasks (IP_Quiz, IP_Exam, IP_Match, MMLU) to highlight IP-specific strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: MMLU
rubrics_metrics.description: Massive Multitask Language Understanding benchmark designed to assess a model’s performance across a diverse set of tasks and subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A higher score reflects versatility and robustness in handling a broad array of language-understanding tasks; used to compare general capabilities versus IP-specialized capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent writing benchmark (dataset coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: A test set of 1,000 instances sampled from all eight major IPC categories covering industries such as chemistry, mechanical engineering, electronics, and biotechnology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to write patentable concept texts; prompts used for generation are provided (Appendix C). Ensures cross-domain coverage for patent-text generation evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BERTScore
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated metric reported for generated patent texts (Table 4/5/6): measures semantic similarity between generated and reference texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher BERTScore suggests better understanding of domain-specific terminology and conceptual depth required for patent writing; used as a primary automated semantic quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLEU-4
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated n-gram precision metric (BLEU-4) used to evaluate the precision and syntactic coherence of generated patent content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher BLEU-4 indicates better precision/syntactic match to reference patent texts; authors report large differences across training strategies (e.g., KPT+SFT+RLHF yields much higher BLEU-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE metrics (ROUGE-1 / ROUGE-2 / ROUGE-L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recall-oriented automated metrics used to evaluate how well generated text mirrors stylistic and structural elements of real patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently higher ROUGE scores indicate accurate and fluent generation that closely matches reference patent stylistic/structural elements; reported alongside BERTScore and BLEU-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Generation Evaluation — Reasonability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonability is assessed as the conformity of generated initial concept texts to USPTO standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-stage approach: randomly select samples (100) and use an advanced LLM (ChatGPT-4) as a judge to determine whether generated initial concept texts meet reasonability; results are reported as Win/Loss (e.g., PatentGPT has a 95% win rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Generation Evaluation — Innovation (Average Rareness Score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is quantified by the Average Rareness Score, which measures novelty by calculating knowledge distance from existing concept combinations in patent databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After filtering for reasonability (USPTO-conforming texts), innovation is assessed using the TechNet evaluation method: a higher score indicates greater novelty/uniqueness relative to existing patents (PatentGPT achieved 0.578 vs lower baselines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Win/Loss (pairwise preference) for reasonability
rubrics_metrics.description: A Win/Loss metric indicating whether a generated concept meets reasonability compared to baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the ChatGPT4 judging setup; reported as win rate (e.g., PatentGPT 95%), providing a comparative human/LLM-judged reasonability signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title quality: specificity and contextual relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should exhibit high specificity and contextual relevance by clearly identifying system structure and function (example: 'engine-transmission connection system' + 'control method').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good titles avoid redundancy, align with industry-specific terminology, and help define patent scope adequately; used in case study comparison between PatentGPT and ChatGPT-4o.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract quality: technical comprehensiveness and application orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts should provide technically comprehensive and application-oriented descriptions that explicitly mention operational details and practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong abstract positions the invention within a practical context (e.g., 'dynamic management of power distribution'), increasing relevance to professionals and examiners and better conveying novelty and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims quality: independent/dependent structure, hierarchical organization, and comprehensive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should include robust independent claims defining system and method, dependent claims elaborating specific features, and a well-organized hierarchical structure ensuring clear coverage of technical aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality claims provide legal robustness and technical applicability (e.g., cover regenerative braking, load balancing, mode transitions); omissions of detailed scenarios weaken legal defensibility as shown in case study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training-component contribution (KPT / SFT / RLHF ablation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the contribution of knowledge-injected pre-training (KPT), supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and RLHF by ablation: measure how removing each stage affects automated metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors report that KPT is an indispensable foundation (removing KPT severely deteriorates performance); SFT critically improves BLEU/ROUGE, and RLHF provides smaller refinements. Use percentage drops in metrics to quantify contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional compliance and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated patent text must comply with jurisdictional variations in patent laws and drafting conventions (claim structure, count restrictions, procedural norms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because training data were primarily USPTO patents, evaluation should check for regional legal requirements (EPO, JPO, CNIPA, etc.); authors recommend retrieval-augmented generation, jurisdiction-specific prompts, and cross-jurisdictional datasets to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty/legal patentability and plagiarism risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative novelty scores do not replace legal assessments of originality and patentability; there is risk that models may generate text resembling existing patents (unintentional plagiarism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend integrating qualitative evaluations by patent attorneys to assess patentability, sufficiency of disclosure, and compliance with regional laws; novelty metrics should be complemented by legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to emerging technical domains (technical accuracy / hallucination risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Models must have up-to-date knowledge for emerging fields (quantum computing, BCIs, synthetic biology) to avoid generating hallucinated or technically inaccurate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note limited coverage in training data (patents 2021–2022) and recommend continuous knowledge updates and external retrieval mechanisms to improve domain adaptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical, economic, and governance considerations for generated patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation should include higher-level assessment of potential misuse (excessive/low-quality filings), democratization effects, job displacement, and policy implications of AI-generated patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors urge development of technology policies, AI auditing frameworks to detect unethical filing, engagement with patent offices/policymakers, and balanced approaches that maintain human accountability while leveraging AI capabilities.
